{{short description|British producer of snacks}} {{Use British English|date=March 2024}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2015}} {{Infobox company | name = KP Snacks Limited | logo = | former_name = {{Ubli | Is Brazil Limited
(Nov{{endash}}Dec 2012) | Top Snacks Limited (2012{{endash}}2013){{Cite web |date=2012-11-30 |title=KP Snacks Limited |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/08314505 |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=[[Companies House]] |language=en}} }} | type = [[Limited company|Limited]] | area_served = United Kingdom | founded = {{start date and age|1853|df=yes}} | hq_location = [[Slough]], England | industry = {{Ubl | [[Snack]]s | [[Peanut]]s }} | products = {{Ubl | Nuts | [[Potato chips|Crisps]] }} | owner = [[Intersnack]] | website = {{URL|kpsnacks.com}} }} '''KP Snacks Limited''' is a British producer of branded and own-label maize-, potato-, and nut-based [[Snack foods|snacks]]. Originating in 1853 in [[Rotherham]], [[West Riding of Yorkshire]], the KP stands for "Kenyon Produce". KP Snacks has been owned by the German company [[Intersnack]] since 2012 and is now based in [[Slough]].{{Cite web |title=Our Story - KP Snacks |url=https://www.kpsnacks.com/about-us/our-story |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=www.kpsnacks.com}} KP Snacks is currently the second largest maker of snack foods in Britain. It owns and produces various brands including KP Nuts, [[Hula Hoops]], [[McCoy's (crisp)|McCoy's]] crisps and [[Tyrrells (crisps)|Tyrrells]] crisps,{{Cite news |date=2012-12-05 |title=KP Nuts snacks firm sold to German company |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-20607637 |access-date=2025-10-05 |work=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |last=Bernard |first=Dominic |title=KP Snacks attributes growth and higher profits to solid brand performance |url=https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/news/kp-snacks-attributes-growth-and-higher-profits-to-solid-brand-performance/710206.article |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=The Grocer |language=en}} and also distributes other brands under license in the country such as [[Pom-Bear]]. The company's largest factory is located in [[Teesside]].{{Cite web |date=2019-05-23 |title=NEW £6M FACILITY OPENS AT KP SNACKS TEESSIDE AS THE SITE COMMEMORATES ITS 50TH ANNIVERSARY |url=https://www.kpsnacks.com/news/show/new-pound6m-facility-opens-at-kp-snacks-teesside-as-the-site-commemorates-its-50th-anniversary |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=www.kpsnacks.com |language=en-GB}} ==History== The company was founded in [[Rotherham]] in 1853 as Kenyon & Son as a producer of confectionery, [[Fruit preserves#Jam|jam]] and [[Pickling|pickles]]. By 1891 the company had become Kenyon & Son and Craven Limited. The company switched to producing roasted and salted [[Corylus avellana|hazelnuts]] in 1948, expanding to peanuts later. These were originally produced for sale in cinemas. In 1952 the company introduced ''Hercules Nuts'' and in 1953 the ''No.1 KP Nuts'' peanut brand. [[File:KP Snacks (logo).png|thumb|Logo used for the namesake nuts and snacks]] The company became part of [[United Biscuits]] (UB) in 1968. The KP Snacks subsidiary produces a range of packet snack brands including [[Hula Hoops]], [[Skips (snack)|Skips]], [[McCoy's (crisp)|McCoy's]], Frisps, Brannigan's, Royster's, [[Space Raiders (snack food)|Space Raiders]], [[Nik Naks (British snack)|Nik Naks]], [[Wheat Crunchies]], Discos, and [[Phileas Fogg snacks|Phileas Fogg.]]{{cite web |title=KP Snacks |url=http://www.kpsnacks.com/ |accessdate=26 October 2014}} The ''snacks'' part is based on [[Teesside]] and in Rotherham, near the UB distribution warehouse. The [[Ashby-de-la-Zouch]] site won a Best Factory Award in 2004.{{cite web|url=http://www.bestfactoryawards.co.uk/awards/2004/BFA/KP.htm|title=Best Factory Awards|publisher=}} UB sold the company to the German company [[Intersnack]] in December 2012 for £500 million.{{cite news |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/business/business-news/kp-snacks-snapped-up-intersnack-698388 |title=KP Snacks snapped up by Intersnack in £500m deal|date=5 December 2012 |work=[[Manchester Evening News]]}} The company moved its headquarters to [[Slough]] in 2015.{{Cite web |date=2015-09-24 |title=Snacks giant moves into new home in Slough |url=https://www.sloughobserver.co.uk/news/13781152.kp-snacks-move-into-new-slough-home/ |access-date=2025-10-05 |website=Slough Observer |language=en}} In February 2022, it was reported that the KP Snacks supply chain was affected by a ransomware attack.{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-60230077|title = KP Snacks hack prompts crisp and nut supplies warning|work = BBC News|date = 3 February 2022}} In July 2023, workers threatened to strike because of low wages despite KP Snacks registering profits of £54 million. [[Unite the Union|Unite union]] reported that the average pay at KP Snacks had fallen by 14% in real terms since 2018.{{Cite web |title=KP Snacks: Possibility of peanut shortage as workers threaten strikes|url=https://news.sky.com/story/kp-snacks-possibility-of-peanut-shortage-as-workers-threaten-strikes-12922695 |access-date=2023-07-18 |website=Sky News |language=en}} ==Sourcing== As a group, they are the largest buyer of nuts in the world (as of 2019),{{cite web|url=https://www.kpnuts.com/sustainability/|title=Sustainability|website=KP Nuts}} sourcing from Asia, Africa, South America and Central America. They have various local aid and sustainability projects. ==Brands== This is a list of snack brands distributed by KP Snacks including some that are not owned by it. KP Snacks Limited is a British producer of branded and own-label maize-, potato-, and nut-based snacks. Originating in 1853 in Rotherham, West Riding of Yorkshire, the KP stands for "Kenyon Produce". KP Snacks has been owned by the German company Intersnack since 2012 and is now based in Slough.
KP Snacks is currently the second largest maker of snack foods in Britain. It owns and produces various brands including KP Nuts, Hula Hoops, McCoy's crisps and Tyrrells crisps, and also distributes other brands under license in the country such as Pom-Bear. The company's largest factory is located in Teesside.
